title: Portuguese sight the Mascarenes
description: Diogo Fernandes Pereira's ship, blown off course from a fleet bound for India, becomes the first European vessel to report the uninhabited island the Portuguese call Ilha do Cirne.

title: Dutch name the island Mauritius
description: Admirals van Neck and van Warwyck land on the island and the Dutch rename it after Maurice of Nassau, Prince of Orange.

title: Dutch settlement begins
description: Cornelius Gooyer founds the first permanent settlement on Mauritius for the Dutch East India Company.

title: Last sighting of the dodo
description: Shipwrecked sailor Volkert Evertsz reports the last widely accepted sighting of the dodo, the bird whose disappearance made "dead as a dodo" a byword for extinction.

title: Dutch abandon the island
description: Worn down by cyclones, pests and poor supply, the Dutch East India Company evacuates its colony.

title: French take possession
description: Guillaume Dufresne d'Arsel lands and claims the abandoned island for France, which renames it the Isle de France.

title: La Bourdonnais arrives
description: Governor Mahé de La Bourdonnais begins the real development of the island, building Port Louis into a naval base and founding its sugar economy.

title: Battle of Grand Port
description: A French squadron beats a British frigate force in the only French naval victory of the Napoleonic Wars.

title: British take the island
description: Months after their defeat at Grand Port the British land in strength from Rodrigues and the French capitulate.

title: Treaty of Paris
description: France formally cedes the island, renamed Mauritius again, together with Rodrigues and the Seychelles, to Great Britain.

title: First indentured labourers
description: The first Indian indentured workers land at Port Louis to work the sugar estates, the start of a migration that reshapes the island's society.

title: Slavery abolished
description: The abolition of slavery becomes effective in Mauritius, freeing tens of thousands of enslaved Africans and Malagasy.

title: First legislative elections
description: Elections for the new Legislative Council, with the franchise widened beyond the planter class, start the road to self-rule.

title: Chagos detached
description: As a condition of independence discussions Britain separates the Chagos Archipelago from Mauritius to form the British Indian Ocean Territory, a dispute Mauritius still pursues.

title: Independence party wins
description: Ramgoolam's coalition campaigning for independence wins a majority in the general election.

title: Independence
description: Mauritius becomes independent within the Commonwealth with Seewoosagur Ramgoolam as prime minister, the date chosen to match Gandhi's Salt March.

title: Jugnauth landslide
description: The young militants of the MMM-PSM coalition win every contested seat in parliament and make Anerood Jugnauth prime minister.

title: Republic proclaimed
description: Exactly twenty-four years after independence, Mauritius becomes a republic within the Commonwealth with a president replacing the Queen.

title: Kaya riots
description: The death in police custody of the singer Kaya, a hero of the Creole community, triggers days of deadly rioting across the island.
